title: The same gate, with and without MCP
measures: One model (base Qwen3-8B, temperature 0), 13 tasks (6 everyday, 7 traps) and a superuser oracle that compares every table before and after each task. Only the connection changes: native (one SQL statement through pg_agent_gate), native-loop (the same, agentic), gated-mcp (the same gate over MCP) and stock-mcp (a popular Postgres MCP server with the same privileges and no gate). Reported per arm: good tasks done, trap breaches, prompt tokens, model calls, median seconds per task, errors.
caveats: 13 tasks is a demonstration, not a statistical benchmark; repeat=3 shows run-to-run variation.

The model server runs with a 4096-token context window. The MCP arms carry tool definitions and tool results inside it; in the cited run one gated-mcp error was a context overflow. A larger window would likely change the MCP arms' numbers.
Times come only from clean GitHub runners; times from a shared machine are never cited.
The cited run measured pg_agent_gate 0.4.0 on PostgreSQL 18; the public image ships 0.4.1 on PostgreSQL 19rc1. config=current measures 0.4.1.
